aria: Animated recap of the Knicks' 113 to 106 home win over the Pacers: Karl-Anthony Towns' 33-foot 3-pointer with 54 seconds left in the third quarter that made it 86 to 74, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Towns' 30 points and 13 rebounds, the top scorers, how the Knicks won, and the next game.
notes: Box score from the Knicks' 113–106 home win over the Indiana Pacers on Nov 22, 2026, from the Covers box score, checked line for line against the StatMuse game page. All 113 New York points and all 106 Indiana points add up from the player lines. The quarter scores (26–29–34–24 to 26–25–27–28) add up to both totals: New York led 55–51 at the half and 89–78 after three. Points in the paint (42–56) and both biggest leads (New York 15, Indiana 7) are from Covers and StatMuse; threes (15 of 43 to 6 of 23), assists (30–20), rebounds (50–42), offensive rebounds (12–7) and free throws (16 of 22 to 28 of 33) are from both box scores. Josh Hart's 10 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists are from both box scores (the AP story has 10 rebounds and 11 assists). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games.

Karl-Anthony Towns outscored Indiana 10–2 in the closing minutes of the third quarter, ending with a 3-pointer that made it 86–74 with 54 seconds left (AP); the StatMuse play-by-play has the run from 2:04 (free throws, a floater, a three-point play and the three, assisted by Josh Hart). Jalen Brunson's fadeaway made it 110–95 with 2:35 left, New York's largest lead (AP; StatMuse). Indiana scored the next six, capped by Obi Toppin's basket with 25 seconds left (112–106; AP; StatMuse shows 0:24), and Brunson's free throw made it 113–106 (AP; StatMuse). It was New York's fifth straight win (AP; Ball Exclusives via Yardbarker). Towns had missed Saturday's game with an illness; OG Anunoby missed his second straight game (AP). The Knicks host Cleveland on Wednesday (AP; Ball Exclusives).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Towns' 3-pointer, logged on the StatMuse play-by-play as a 33-foot running three assisted by Josh Hart, which turned 83–74 into 86–74. It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc; the run-up and the exact spot on the floor are not drawn. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the New York Knicks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Towns' listed 7-foot and 248 pounds, with his arms scaled to a measured 7-foot-3½ wingspan (DraftExpress, 2014 Nike Hoop Summit), No. 32 (RealGM), in New York's home white with his look from the look sheet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
